title: Evaluating a Multivariable Limit via Polar Coordinates
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Evaluate lim_{(x, y) -> (0, 0)} (x^3 + y^3) / (x^2 + y^2) using polar coordinates.

steps.title: Convert to Polar Coordinates
steps.mathExpression: x = r\cos\theta, \; y = r\sin\theta \implies \frac{x^3 + y^3}{x^2 + y^2} = \frac{r^3(\cos^3\theta + \sin^3\theta)}{r^2} = r(\cos^3\theta + \sin^3\theta)
steps.explanation: Substitute polar expressions and simplify powers of r.
steps.why: Isolating radial distance from angular orientation.

steps.title: Evaluate Limit as r -> 0
steps.explanation: Since the angular term is bounded by 2, the product approaches 0 uniformly in theta.
